provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Reading fluency
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read a page without stopping.
The pupils should be able to pause at punctuation marks.
Introduction:
We have learned to read words. Today we will read pages.
Reading pages fast makes us good readers.
Content:
Reading fluency means reading fast and smooth.
We pause at full stops. We take a breath.
We read with expression like storytellers.
Class activity:
Each pupil reads one page from our book.
The class claps for good reading.
Evaluation questions:
What is reading fluency?
Where do we pause when reading?
Read this sentence with a pause at the full stop.
Summary:
Good readers read fast and stop at punctuation.

topics.title: Comprehension 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer who questions.
The pupils should be able to answer what questions.
Introduction:
We have learned to read stories. Today we will answer questions.
Questions help us understand stories better.
Content:
Who questions ask about people in the story.
What questions ask about things that happen.
We listen carefully to find answers.
Class activity:
The teacher reads a story about a market.
Pupils raise hands for who and what questions.
Evaluation questions:
Who went to the market?
What did Mama buy?
Ask a who question about the story.
Summary:
We can answer who and what questions about stories.

topics.title: Comprehension 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer where questions.
The pupils should be able to answer when questions.
Introduction:
We answered who and what questions last week.
Today we will find where and when in stories.
Content:
Where questions ask about places in the story.
When questions ask about time of events.
We look for clues in the story to find answers.
Class activity:
Pupils look at a picture story about a school day.
They point to where and when things happen.
Evaluation questions:
Where did the children play?
When did they eat lunch?
Find a when question in the story.
Summary:
We can find where and when answers in stories.

topics.title: Opposites and rhymes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify opposite pairs.
The pupils should be able to match rhyming words.
Introduction:
We have learned many words. Some words are opposites.
Some words sound the same at the end.
Content:
Opposites have different meanings.
Big and little are opposites.
Day and night are opposites.
Rhyming words sound alike.
Cat and hat rhyme.
Class activity:
The teacher calls out a word. Pupils say the opposite.
Pupils play a rhyming word game with claps.
Evaluation questions:
What is the opposite of hot?
Find a word that rhymes with sun.
Name two opposite words.
Summary:
Opposites are different. Rhymes sound alike.

topics.title: Simple writing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write their name.
The pupils should be able to write their age and class.
Introduction:
We have learned to read words. Today we will write about ourselves.
Writing our name is very important.
Content:
We write our name with big letters.
We write our age with numbers.
We write our class name.
We can write one sentence about ourselves.
Class activity:
Each pupil writes their name on a card.
They practice writing their age and class.
Evaluation questions:
How do you write your name?
What class are you in?
Write one sentence about yourself.
Summary:
We can write our name and one sentence about us.

topics.title: Picture composition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to look at a picture.
The pupils should be able to write two sentences about what they see.
Introduction:
We have written about ourselves. Today we will write about pictures.
Pictures tell stories we can write about.
Content:
Look at all the things in the picture.
What do you see? Who is there?
Write two sentences about what you see.
Use words like big, small, happy, sad.
Class activity:
The teacher shows a picture of a market scene.
Pupils take turns to say what they see.
Then they write two sentences about it.
Evaluation questions:
What do you see in the picture?
Write one sentence about the picture.
Who is in the picture?
Summary:
We can write sentences about what we see in pictures.

topics.title: Story writing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write a three sentence story.
The pupils should be able to use first, then, last.
Introduction:
We have written about pictures. Today we will write our own stories.
Stories have beginning, middle and end.
Content:
A story has three parts.
First tells what happened first.
Then tells what happened next.
Last tells what happened at the end.
We write three sentences for our story.
Class activity:
The teacher tells a story about a lost shoe.
Pupils write their own three sentence story about something lost.
Evaluation questions:
What comes first in a story?
How many sentences in our story?
Write the first sentence of your story.
Summary:
We can write three sentence stories with first, then, last.

topics.title: Spelling drill
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to spell family words.
The pupils should be able to use look, cover, write, check.
Introduction:
We have written stories. Today we will learn to spell words.
Spelling means writing words correctly.
Content:
Family words are words about family.
Mama, Papa, Brother, Sister, Child.
Look at the word, cover it, write it, check it.
This helps us remember how to spell.
Class activity:
The teacher says a family word.
Pupils spell it using look, cover, write, check method.
Evaluation questions:
Spell the word Mama.
What is the look, cover, write, check method?
Spell one family word.
Summary:
We can spell family words with look, cover, write, check.

topics.title: Dictionary fun
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to find words in a picture dictionary.
The pupils should be able to play the find the word game.
Introduction:
We have learned many words. Today we will use a dictionary.
A dictionary has words in order from A to Z.
Content:
A dictionary helps us find words.
Words are in ABC order.
Picture dictionaries have pictures with words.
We can find any word if we know its first letter.
Class activity:
The teacher calls out a word.
Pupils find it in the picture dictionary and point to it.
Evaluation questions:
What is a dictionary?
How are words in a dictionary?
Find the word apple in the dictionary.
Summary:
We can find words in a picture dictionary.

topics.title: Revision and reading graduation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read a full story alone.
The pupils should be able to get a reading certificate.
Introduction:
We have learned to read and write all term. Today we will show what we know.
Reading graduation is a celebration of our reading skills.
Content:
We will read a full story by ourselves.
We will use all our reading skills.
We will get a certificate for good reading.
The certificate shows we are good readers.
Class activity:
Each pupil reads a story to the teacher.
The class claps for each reader.
Evaluation questions:
Can you read this story?
What will you get for reading well?
Read your favorite part of the story.
Summary:
We are good readers and we get certificates.
